mcu_0160_08001e18.name: mcu_param_block3_init_checked
mcu_0160_08001e18.summary: Validate and fill a 3-word parameter block, setting a valid flag at +0x2c
mcu_0160_08001e18.description: Accepts (block, a, b, c). If a != 0, 0 <= b <= 0x40000000 and c >= 0 it stores a, b, c into words 0..2 of the block, clears word 3 (a running/accumulator value) and sets the byte at offset 0x2c (param_1+0xb words) to 1, returning 1. Otherwise it only clears the valid byte at +0x2c and returns 0. Looks like the init routine of a controller/filter object (gain, limit, initial value); called once from the larger setup function mcu_0160_080029ac together with mcu_0160_08002a34. Exact meaning of the three fields is not visible here.

params.name: param_1
params.description: block to initialise (>= 0x30 bytes; word0..2 params, word3 state, byte at +0x2c = valid)

params.name: param_2
params.description: must be non-zero, stored in word 0

mcu_0160_08001e18.notes: Role of the block (probably a PI/limiter or filter object) is a guess; behaviour itself is certain.

mcu_0160_08002078.name: mcu_scale_delta_q15
mcu_0160_08002078.summary: Return (DAT_20000f5a - DAT_2000027e) * 0xdbf using Q15 fixed-point arithmetic
mcu_0160_08002078.description: Computes the unsigned 16-bit difference of two RAM values (0x20000f5a minus 0x2000027e, e.g. a measured value minus its offset/reference), shifts it into Q15 (<<15) and multiplies by the Q15 constant 0xdbf (3519, about 0.1074) using a 64-bit signed multiply, then shifts the 64-bit product right by 15. The net result is delta * 3519, i.e. a fixed-point rescale of a raw count difference. Called from mcu_0160_08005d84. The same Q15 pattern (0x8000 = 1.0) is used by the neighbouring helpers in this group.
mcu_0160_08002078.notes: What the two RAM values physically are (ADC counts? current offset?) is not determinable from this function alone.

mcu_0160_080021fc.name: mcu_get_var_f60
mcu_0160_080021fc.summary: Getter returning the 16-bit RAM value at 0x20000f60
mcu_0160_080021fc.description: Returns DAT_20000f60 unchanged (zero-extended 16-bit load). Called only from mcu_0160_0800a90c. Pure accessor used so other modules do not touch the variable directly.

mcu_0160_08002208.name: mcu_mul_q15_f5e_by_3f2
mcu_0160_08002208.summary: Q15 multiply of RAM value 0x20000f5e (shifted to Q15) by 0x200003f2, result >> 15
mcu_0160_08002208.description: Loads the 16-bit value at 0x20000f5e, shifts it left by 15 (so it is treated as an integer in Q15), multiplies it by the 16-bit value at 0x200003f2 with a 64-bit signed multiply and returns the product >> 15, i.e. effectively f5e * 3f2 without overflow. Called from mcu_0160_08005b3c (and the 12b equivalent). Acts as a gain/scale step; the second operand is probably a calibration or configuration scale factor.
mcu_0160_08002208.notes: Operand meanings unknown; arithmetic is certain.

mcu_0160_08002890.name: mcu_add_overflow_direction_s32
mcu_0160_08002890.summary: Report whether a + b would overflow int32 (+1 positive, -1 negative, 0 none)
mcu_0160_08002890.description: Pre-checks a signed 32-bit addition without performing it. Returns 1 if both operands are positive and b > INT_MAX - a (positive overflow), -1 (0xffffffff) if both are negative and a < INT_MIN - b (negative overflow), otherwise 0. Used by mcu_0160_08003c78 (accumulator / integrator saturation logic) to decide when to clamp.

mcu_0160_08002946.name: mcu_array_max_s32
mcu_0160_08002946.summary: Maximum of an int32 array of n elements
mcu_0160_08002946.description: Linear scan: starts with element 0 and keeps the largest of elements 1..n-1. The decompiler dropped the return statement but the running maximum is left in the return register, so the function returns the maximum (for n <= 1 it returns element 0). Called by mcu_0160_08002148. Companion of mcu_array_min_s32 (mcu_0160_08002964).
mcu_0160_08002946.notes: Return value inferred from register allocation; decompiler shows void.

mcu_0160_08002964.name: mcu_array_min_s32
mcu_0160_08002964.summary: Minimum of an int32 array of n elements
mcu_0160_08002964.description: Linear scan returning the smallest of elements 0..n-1 (decompiler shows void but the running minimum stays in r0). Called by mcu_0160_0800209c. Companion of mcu_array_max_s32 (mcu_0160_08002946).
mcu_0160_08002964.notes: Return value inferred from register allocation.

mcu_0160_08002982.name: mcu_ramp_toward_target_s32
mcu_0160_08002982.summary: Move *value toward target by at most |step| (slew-rate limiter)
mcu_0160_08002982.description: Takes the absolute value of step, then if *value is above target by more than step subtracts step, else if below target by more than step adds step, otherwise snaps *value to target exactly. Implements a per-call rate limit (ramp) on a 32-bit signed quantity, e.g. a torque/current/speed command. Called from four places (mcu_0160_08003434, 08003f2c, 0800adf0, 0800b10c), the control-loop code.

params.name: param_2
params.description: pointer to the current value (s32), updated in place

mcu_12b_080029ce.name: mcu_limit_ramp_update
mcu_12b_080029ce.summary: Update a ramped limit (halve/x1.2 on flag change, +0x1999 per call) and clamp an output
mcu_12b_080029ce.description: Works on a control object: byte flag at +0xbc (current limiting/fault request), byte at +0xbd (previous flag state) and the int limit state at +0xa0. On a 0->1 edge of the flag the stored limit is halved; on a 1->0 edge it is multiplied by 0x9999/0x8000 (about 1.2, Q15). The previous flag is then updated. If the flag is clear, the limit is raised by 0x1999 (about 0.2 in Q15) per call but not above the ceiling param_2 and stored back; if the flag is set the working limit is 0. When param_4 is non-zero the limit is applied to *param_3 as *param_3 = min(*param_3, limit) (so a set flag forces it to 0 or below) and the function returns 1 if the flag is set, else 0. Only present in the 12b build; later builds restructured it (see the plain getter mcu_152_08002a18 / mcu_0160_08002a20 neighbours).

params.name: param_1
params.description: control object (fields at +0xa0 limit, +0xbc flag, +0xbd previous flag)

params.name: param_2
params.description: upper ceiling for the ramped limit

params.name: param_3
params.description: in/out command (s32) clamped by the limit

params.name: param_4
params.description: non-zero to apply the limit to *param_3

returns.description: 1 if clamping was applied while the flag is set, else 0

mcu_12b_080029ce.notes: Interpretation as a current/torque derating limit is a guess from structure; no direct callers (indirect or inlined).

mcu_152_08002a18.name: mcu_ctx_get_field_0x90
mcu_152_08002a18.summary: Getter returning the 32-bit field at offset 0x90 of a context struct
mcu_152_08002a18.description: Returns *(u32 *)(param_1 + 0x90). Plain accessor on the same large control/context object that mcu_12b_080029ce indexes (offsets 0xa0, 0xbc, 0xbd). No direct callers (called through a pointer table or tail position). Present in the 143 and 152 builds.

mcu_0160_08002a20.name: mcu_select_stack_local_fragment
mcu_0160_08002a20.summary: Code fragment: pick one of two caller stack slots depending on a third
mcu_0160_08002a20.description: Not a true function: the decompiler shows reads of in_stack_00000030, in_stack_000000c8 and in_stack_000000d0, i.e. it uses the stack frame of its caller (mcu_0160_08002b64) without setting up its own. Logic: if the slot at sp+0xd0 is non-zero return the slot at sp+0xc8, otherwise the slot at sp+0x30. It is a compiler-split tail/outlined block of the enclosing routine. The 12b build has the equivalent mcu_12b_08002c00.
mcu_0160_08002a20.notes: Outlined fragment sharing its caller's frame; do not treat as a standalone API.

mcu_0160_08002a34.name: mcu_param_block8_init_checked
mcu_0160_08002a34.summary: Fill an 8-word parameter block if the first and third values are positive
mcu_0160_08002a34.description: If param_4 > 0 and param_2 > 0, copies the eight input values param_2..param_9 into words 0..7 of the block param_1 and returns 1; otherwise leaves the block untouched and returns 0. Nine arguments (the last five on the stack). Called from the same setup function mcu_0160_080029ac as mcu_param_block3_init_checked; group of parameter-block initialisers for controller objects (cf. mcu_12b_08002c0e, a 4-word predecessor).

mcu_12b_08002c00.name: mcu_12b_select_stack_local_fragment
mcu_12b_08002c00.summary: Code fragment (12b build): conditionally replace one caller stack slot with another
mcu_12b_08002c00.description: Uses the stack frame of its callers (mcu_12b_08002a3c, mcu_12b_08002d0c) without its own frame: if the slot at sp+0xb8 is zero the slot at sp+0xb0 is overwritten with the slot at sp+0x20; the slot at sp+0xb0 is then returned. Outlined common tail of two routines. Equivalent of mcu_0160_08002a20 in the later builds (different frame offsets).

returns.description: value of the stack slot at sp+0xb0 after the optional replacement

mcu_12b_08002c00.notes: Fragment that shares the callers' frame.

mcu_12b_08002c0e.name: mcu_param_block4_init_checked
mcu_12b_08002c0e.summary: Fill a 4-word parameter block if the first two values are positive
mcu_12b_08002c0e.description: If param_3 > 0 and param_2 > 0 stores param_2..param_5 in words 0..3 of the block and returns 1, else returns 0 without modification. 12b-build predecessor of mcu_param_block8_init_checked (mcu_0160_08002a34); called from mcu_12b_08002b70.

mcu_0160_08002ec8.name: mcu_bits_clear
mcu_0160_08002ec8.description: Read-modify-write helper that clears the bits given in mask in the 32-bit word at p. Called from many places (mcu_0160_08005a00, 08005ab0, 08007dc8 and the 12b equivalents) that manage flag/state words; the generated-code style (tiny helper for every bit operation) suggests machine-generated control code. Group with mcu_bits_and and mcu_bits_set.

mcu_0160_08002ed2.name: mcu_bits_and
mcu_0160_08002ed2.summary: Return a & b (bitwise AND of two words)
mcu_0160_08002ed2.description: Trivial helper returning param_1 & param_2; used by mcu_0160_08004e48, 080061fc and 0800854c to test flag bits. Group with mcu_bits_clear and mcu_bits_set.

mcu_0160_08002ed6.name: mcu_bits_set
mcu_0160_08002ed6.description: Read-modify-write helper that ORs mask into the 32-bit word at p. Called from nine routines (mcu_0160_08005a00, 08005a58, 08005ab0, 08005b3c, 08007364 and the 12b equivalents), all of which set flags in state words. Group with mcu_bits_clear and mcu_bits_and.

mcu_0160_08003034.name: mcu_hall_state_dispatch
mcu_0160_08003034.summary: Dispatch to a per-state handler selected by bits 9..11 of a status word
mcu_0160_08003034.description: Extracts idx = (DAT_20001fda & 0xfff) >> 9 (a 3-bit value 0..7, most likely the Hall-sensor pattern) and calls the function pointer at 0x20000698[idx] (a RAM table of 8 handlers) with argument DAT_20000678 ^ idx, i.e. the bit mask of what changed since the previous state. It then stores the new index (same bit field 9..11 re-extracted) into DAT_20000678 as the previous state. Called from mcu_0160_08007268, an interrupt-level routine. A Hall-commutation/edge interpretation is a guess based on the 3-bit field.
mcu_0160_08003034.notes: 0x20000698 is address-taken: an 8-entry function-pointer table in RAM. Actual source of 0x20001fda (Hall inputs vs. captured timer value) not shown.

mcu_0160_080032c8.name: BusFault_Handler
mcu_0160_080032c8.summary: Cortex-M BusFault exception handler: infinite loop
mcu_0160_080032c8.description: Vector table handler for BusFault; spins forever (b .), so a bus error hangs the CPU until the independent watchdog resets it. No logging or recovery. Present in the 143, 152 and 0160 builds (shared with other fault handlers that loop in the same manner).

mcu_0160_08003624.name: mcu_status_bf4_any_low_bits
mcu_0160_08003624.summary: Return 1 if either of the low two bits of status byte 0x20000bf4 is set
mcu_0160_08003624.description: Normalises (DAT_20000bf4 & 3) to a boolean. The byte is a state/fault bitfield; callers are the main control routines mcu_0160_08003f2c, 080052bc and 08005978. Which conditions bits 0 and 1 stand for is unknown.

returns.description: 1 if bit0 or bit1 set, else 0

mcu_0160_08003638.name: mcu_below_10pct_of_window
mcu_0160_08003638.summary: Return 1 if a Q15-scaled value lies in the lowest 10% of the window [DAT_20000bee, DAT_20000bec]
mcu_0160_08003638.description: Computes (param_1 - bee * 0x8000) / (bec - bee + 1) with signed 32-bit division, where bee and bec are 16-bit RAM values (low and high bounds) and param_1 is the input scaled by 0x8000. That yields the position within the window as a Q15 fraction; returns 1 if it is below 0xccc (3276, about 0.0999 = 10%), else 0. Called from mcu_0160_08005090 and 080051bc (and mcu_12b_08004e74).

params.name: param_1
params.description: value in Q15 (raw * 0x8000) to test against the window

returns.description: 1 if in the lowest 10% of the window

mcu_0160_08003638.notes: Interpretation of the window (speed/throttle/torque range) unknown.

mcu_0160_080046cc.name: mcu_get_cfg_field_0x28
mcu_0160_080046cc.summary: Return the 32-bit field at offset 0x28 of the struct pointed to by DAT_200000f8
mcu_0160_080046cc.description: DAT_200000f8 holds a pointer to a configuration/state structure; the function returns the word at +0x28. Called from mcu_0160_0800a320 and 0800c6f0. See mcu_0160_080046d8, which reads the same field and passes it through a Q15 multiply by 1.0.

mcu_0160_080046d8.name: mcu_get_cfg_field_0x28_q15
mcu_0160_080046d8.summary: Return field +0x28 of *DAT_200000f8 after a (x * 0x8000) >> 15 round trip
mcu_0160_080046d8.description: Loads the word at *(DAT_200000f8 + 0x28), multiplies it by 0x8000 in 64 bits and shifts the product right by 15, which is an identity (a Q15 multiply by 1.0 left in by the generated code). Returns the same value as mcu_0160_080046cc but is the variant used by the control routines mcu_0160_08003f2c, 08004e78, 080052bc, 08005424 (and mcu_143_080052ac).
mcu_0160_080046d8.notes: Identity operation; the code is evidently generated from a fixed-point model.

mcu_0160_080046f4.name: mcu_get_var_650
mcu_0160_080046f4.summary: Getter returning the 32-bit RAM variable at 0x20000650
mcu_0160_080046f4.description: Returns DAT_20000650. Called from mcu_0160_08003f2c only. Part of a family of getters for parameters stored at 0x2000065x (0x20000654, 0x20000658, 0x20000660 ...) which look like a configuration/status block.

mcu_0160_080047b4.name: mcu_q15_to_percent_s16
mcu_0160_080047b4.summary: Convert the Q15 value at 0x20000a50 to a percentage (x * 100 / 32768) as s16
mcu_0160_080047b4.description: Multiplies DAT_20000a50 (32-bit signed) by 0x320000 (= 100 * 0x8000) in 64 bits, shifts right by 15 (so x * 100) and again by 15 (divide by 0x8000), then truncates to a signed 16-bit result. So 1.0 in Q15 maps to 100. Called from mcu_0160_0800c6f0, the code that builds the externally visible/communicated values.
mcu_0160_080047b4.notes: What 0x20000a50 represents (throttle request? torque fraction?) is not known.

mcu_0160_08004ac4.name: mcu_get_limit_min3_or_unbounded
mcu_0160_08004ac4.summary: Return DAT_20000660 clamped to >= 0x18000, or 0x7fff8000 if it is zero
mcu_0160_08004ac4.description: If the 32-bit value at 0x20000660 is zero the function returns 0x7fff8000, effectively an unlimited maximum (about 65535.0 in Q15). Otherwise it returns the value but never less than 0x18000 (3.0 in Q15). Treats 0 as 'feature/limit disabled' and enforces a floor on configured limits. Called from mcu_0160_08003d2c, 080052bc, 0800576c and 0800ce3c.

returns.description: limit in Q15, minimum 0x18000, 0x7fff8000 when unset

mcu_0160_08004ac4.notes: Physical unit unknown (current, speed or time).

mcu_0160_08004ae4.name: mcu_get_param_654_q15
mcu_0160_08004ae4.summary: Return the byte/halfword at 0x20000654 shifted into Q15 (<< 15)
mcu_0160_08004ae4.description: Zero-extends DAT_20000654 and shifts it left by 15, converting an integer configuration value into Q15 fixed point. Called from mcu_0160_08003f2c, 0800500c, 08005090, 080051bc (and mcu_12b_08004e74).

mcu_0160_08004af0.name: mcu_get_var_67c
mcu_0160_08004af0.summary: Getter returning the 32-bit RAM variable at 0x2000067c
mcu_0160_08004af0.description: Returns DAT_2000067c unchanged. Only present in the 152 and 0160 builds; called from mcu_0160_08005090.

mcu_0160_08004afc.name: mcu_cond_658_and_not_a9a
mcu_0160_08004afc.summary: Return 1 if flag 0x20000658 is non-zero and flag 0x20000a9a is zero
mcu_0160_08004afc.description: Boolean combiner of two RAM bytes: true when the configuration/enable byte DAT_20000658 is non-zero and the inhibit byte DAT_20000a9a is zero. Called from mcu_0160_08003f2c and mcu_0160_080047d0.
mcu_0160_08004afc.notes: Semantics of the two flags unknown; assumed enable/inhibit.

mcu_0160_08004b1c.name: mcu_cond_mode_bit0_and_level_ok
mcu_0160_08004b1c.summary: Return 1 if mode bit0 of 0x2000065d is set and 0x200003ea is at least 10 above both thresholds
mcu_0160_08004b1c.description: True when (DAT_2000065d & 1) != 0 and both signed 16-bit thresholds DAT_20000024 and DAT_20000026 are <= DAT_200003ea - 10 (a 10-count hysteresis/margin). 0x2000065d is a mode/status byte also used by mcu_0160_08004b54 (bit1) and mcu_0160_08005550 (bit2 and bits 3..4). Called from mcu_0160_08003f2c, 0800480c, 08004944, 0800a320 and 0800e238.
mcu_0160_08004b1c.notes: Operands are probably a measured value compared with two limits; unknown which.

mcu_0160_08004b54.name: mcu_mode_bit1_inverted
mcu_0160_08004b54.summary: Return the inverse of bit 1 of mode byte 0x2000065d
mcu_0160_08004b54.description: Returns (~(DAT_2000065d >> 1)) & 1, i.e. 1 when bit 1 of the mode/status byte is clear. Called only from mcu_0160_08003f2c. Companion accessor to mcu_0160_08004b1c (bit 0) and mcu_0160_08005550 (bits 2..4).

mcu_0160_08004e64.name: mcu_flag_1fce_is_clear
mcu_0160_08004e64.summary: Return 1 if the byte at 0x20001fce is zero, else 0
mcu_0160_08004e64.description: Logical-not of DAT_20001fce, returned as 0/1. Callers mcu_0160_080056e4, 08008a14, 0800adf0 and 0800b10c use it as a gating condition (the byte is likely a fault/disable flag). Highly likely 'not faulted/enabled' semantics, but unproven.
mcu_0160_08004e64.notes: Name chosen neutrally; byte meaning unknown.

mcu_0160_08005008.name: mcu_nop_stub
mcu_0160_08005008.description: Single return instruction; a placeholder or optimised-out hook. Called from mcu_0160_08005090 (probably a call to a feature that is compiled out in this build). Present in the 143, 152 and 0160 builds.

mcu_143_08005478.name: mcu_update_motion_flag_old
mcu_143_08005478.summary: Set flag 0x20000dfd when a counter >= 20, |value| <= 0x50000 and mode bit2 is set (12b/143)
mcu_143_08005478.description: If DAT_20000b00 < 20, clears DAT_20000dfd. Otherwise takes abs(DAT_20000f0c); if it is <= 0x50000 (10.0 in Q15) and bit 2 of the mode byte at 0x20000649 is set, sets DAT_20000dfd to 1, else to 0. Older (12b, 143) version of mcu_0160_08005550, which in later builds splits the result into two flags depending on mode bits 3..4. No direct callers (called through a pointer or tail jump).
mcu_143_08005478.notes: Likely 'speed low and stable for N cycles' qualifier; guess. Addresses differ from later builds (0x649 vs 0x65d, dfd vs e1d).

mcu_0160_08005550.name: mcu_update_motion_direction_flags
mcu_0160_08005550.summary: Set one of two flags (0x20000e1d / 0x20000e1e) from mode bits 3..4 when |value| and counter qualify
mcu_0160_08005550.description: Clears both output flags (DAT_20000e1d, DAT_20000e1e) if the counter DAT_20000b20 < 20, if abs(DAT_20000f30) > 0x50000 (10.0 in Q15) or if bit 2 of mode byte 0x2000065d is clear. Otherwise it examines field m = (DAT_2000065d & 0x1f) >> 3 (bits 3..4): m == 2 sets e1d=1 / e1e=0, m == 3 sets e1d=0 / e1e=1, any other value clears both. Called from mcu_0160_08004e78 (a periodic update routine, with mcu_0160_080056c4). Successor of mcu_143_08005478 in the 152 and 0160 builds.
mcu_0160_08005550.notes: The two flags are probably mutually exclusive mode indicators (e.g. forward/reverse or two operating modes); not proven.

mcu_0160_080056c4.name: mcu_update_flag_e32_from_mode_3
mcu_0160_080056c4.summary: Set DAT_20000e32 to 1 when mode byte 0x2000065a equals 3, else 0
mcu_0160_080056c4.description: Single comparison storing (DAT_2000065a == 3) into DAT_20000e32. Called from mcu_0160_08004e78 together with mcu_0160_08005550; part of the group of small per-cycle update routines that derive boolean flags from the configuration/mode bytes at 0x2000065x.
